Write down what was actually run, on what host, and what came out — including the steps that failed and the problems found upstream. A build that succeeded but left no record is not reproducible by anyone else, and a record that omits what went wrong is the failure mode this project exists to avoid.

```day-atom
{"in":["bootable-image","boot-evidence","determinism-result"],"out":["reproduction-record"],"next":["artifact-publication"],"done":["reproduction-record"]}
```

MWE spec was wrong. UserContext has no privilege field; privilege lives on TrapFrame, so P1's struct invariant belongs there. enter and trap both write Privilege::User as a literal, so resume's privilege check is dead under the invariant. The doc's resumable/on_trap signatures do not exist in context.rs.

MWE spec had two substantive errors, both found from the Thermite side. enter drops a mutation: context.rs:97 sets runnable=false before returning the frame, so a sketch returning only the TrapFrame makes the NotRunnable guard dead and breaks the enter/resume cycle P1 and P2 describe. It has to return both halves, as resume does.

create is the richer T0 target and the MWE omitted it. P3 no kernel address, P4 canonical addresses, P5 16-byte stack alignment all come from context.rs:58-90 and are range or bit predicates a wrong constant falsifies concretely. P1 is structurally free via the TrapFrame invariant, so it makes a weak criterion-5 break.
